resources.string: 1×1 squircle coffee cup widget by default — tap to toggle Keep Awake, or resize larger to reveal duration presets (Infinite, 30m, 1h, 2h), Tap Sim toggle, and Settings.
Keeps Googlebook display awake via 1×1 overlay and optional corner micro-taps (no screen reading or data collection).

Awake (by Meridian11 LLC) uses the Android AccessibilityService API solely when you enable Keep-Awake or Simulate Tap/Click Fallback to: (1) maintain a 1×1 transparent keep-screen-on window overlay, and (2) optionally perform a harmless micro-tap at screen coordinate (1, 1) at your chosen interval when standard WakeLocks are restricted by desktop power policies. Awake does NOT read screen content, capture keystrokes, inspect window hierarchies, or collect, store, or transmit any personal or sensitive user data.

To keep your Googlebook or Android desktop awake when enterprise or system policies ignore standard WakeLocks, Awake requests permission to use the Android AccessibilityService API.

• How Awake uses AccessibilityService:
1. Displays an invisible 1×1 pixel window overlay (TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY) with FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON while Awake is active.
2. When 'Simulate Tap / Click Fallback' is turned on, dispatches a single 1-millisecond micro-tap gesture (dispatchGesture) at screen coordinate (1, 1) every 15–120 seconds.

• Privacy & Data Guarantee:
Awake sets canRetrieveWindowContent="false" and listens to zero accessibility events. Awake does NOT read your screen, monitor apps, log keystrokes, or collect, store, or share any personal or sensitive user data. No internet permission is requested.

You can decline now and still use Awake's standard WakeLock mode, or revoke this consent at any time in Awake → About & Legal.
